About Me

Engineering at the crossroads of data and flight.

I'm an Industrial and Robotics Engineering student at Gannon University with a strong interest in aerospace systems. I'm drawn to problems that require both rigorous methodology and creative thinking, from statistical modeling of aerodynamic noise to EU-funded flight trajectory research.

My coursework in Design of Experiments, Statistics, and Strength of Materials has given me a strong analytical foundation, which I've applied to projects spanning airfoil acoustics, ergonomic risk modeling, and time-series forecasting in Python. Most recently, I had the opportunity to contribute to Impact Monitor 2, an EU-funded aviation research program, performing flight trajectory simulations in DYNAMO alongside international research partners.

I bring a multilingual perspective — English, Spanish, Catalan, and French — and experience collaborating across cultures in academic and research environments. I hold certifications in AI fundamentals from IBM and Anthropic, which complement my engineering toolkit.

I'm looking for part-time roles, research opportunities, and graduate programs in aerospace engineering where I can apply my technical and analytical skills to real-world challenges.

GPA: 3.918 / 4.0 B.S. Expected May 2027 EU Research Contributor 2026

Research Interests

Where I want to point my next projects.

Aircraft Design

Conceptual sizing and performance trade studies, building on foundations from DelftX's Introduction to Aeronautical Engineering.

Aerodynamics

Airfoil performance and noise characteristics, extending the NASA self-noise analysis into further test cases.

Sustainable Aviation

Flight trajectory and performance analysis in support of lower-impact aviation, in line with current Impact Monitor 2 research.

Autonomous Systems / Drones

Applying robotics and statistical modeling coursework toward sensing and control for small autonomous platforms.
